# National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES): agent index

NCHS's survey of the health and nutrition of the US civilian noninstitutionalized population, combining interviews with physical examinations and laboratory tests at mobile examination centers. Released in two-year cycles of linked files.

Publisher: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), CDC. Dataset id: `nhanes`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/policy/data-user-agreement.html. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the cycle.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `2015-2016`: 2015-2016; `2017-2020`: 2017-2020; `2021-2023`: 2021-2023. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.

## Across releases

One line per variable across all releases, joined by the links between releases: names and the releases each had ("ADDEPEV2 2011–2018 → ADDEPEV3 2019–2023"). A change of meaning (codes, wording or universe) gives a second line, marked ↳, under the first.
